name: Chogha Golan domesticated-type emmer
description: At Chogha Golan, residents had access to emmer wheat with domestication-type traits in an early agricultural setting.

impact.note: One site's remains showing access to domestic-type emmer in early farming; farming is a new ability, but this site's own legacy is unclear.

date.label: Approximately 9800 cal BP (7850 BCE)
date.basis: Approximate archaeological context; calibrated BP values use 1950 as reference.

events.statement: At Chogha Golan, residents had access to emmer wheat with domestication-type traits in an early agricultural setting.

evidence.supports: The abstract reports domesticated-type emmer around 9800 cal BP in a long local archaeobotanical sequence.

events.caveats: The place of domestication and whether earlier wild cereals were cultivated at this site are disputed; source access was abstract only.
